tested_scope: One bounded authority-domain classification of a second zero-entitlement GitHub public repository or equivalent GitHub account-scoped writable surface as a monotonic witness for target_repository incarnation plus minimum_generation/policy_epoch. Required negatives covered: same principal controls both repositories; witness delete/rewind; target transfer; target delete/recreate under same logical name; connector authorization absent for witness; manual/protected setup. No other worker/downstream/O state was read.

public_sources.observation: GitHub documents that an organization owner or repository administrator can delete a repository; some deleted repositories may be restorable within 90 days. Deleting a public repository does not delete its forks.
GitHub documents that repository admins or roles with edit-repository-rules permission can create, edit and delete repository rulesets; rulesets are available for public repositories on GitHub Free.

GitHub documents that create/update file contents can use a fine-grained token with repository Contents write permission; this is a lightweight file-write path and does not itself require repository Administration permission.
GitHub documents repository transfer between owners, redirects from the previous location, and that creating a new repository/fork at the previous location can permanently remove those redirects.
GitHub Free for organizations supports unlimited public repositories and collaborators; therefore a public witness repository need not add a paid-plan dependency by itself.

authority_matrix.reason: The same principal can delete the witness repository and, as repository admin, can edit/delete its rulesets. A second repository changes location but not rollback authority.
Ruleset availability at zero paid-plan cost does not create authority separation because the repository admin can mutate or delete the ruleset and can delete the repository.

Contents write can be lower privilege than Administration, so target-repository admins need not automatically gain witness-admin authority. However an independently controlled witness owner/protection policy and authorization grant must already exist; establishing or repairing that separation is an external principal/manual-protected setup dependency in the tested scheduled-Chat-only scope.
The current Chat repository transport cannot update a repository it is not authorized to write. Obtaining or expanding authorization is not an automatic role-local scheduled-Chat effect.

If the witness authority can delete or replace its own current history, the minimum-generation lower bound can disappear or roll back. CAS on the current file only detects concurrent version mismatch; it does not make the repository itself monotonic against its administrator.

GitHub transfer changes repository location semantics and a new repository at the previous location can remove redirects. A safe witness must bind an incarnation identifier rather than owner/name alone, and must still survive witness-side rollback. This leaf does not claim GitHub's numeric repository id is a formally permanent anti-recreation identity because the cited transfer documentation does not state that guarantee.

observation_vs_inference.observed: Official docs establish admin deletion authority, ruleset mutability by admins, lower-privilege Contents-write transport, zero-paid-plan availability for public repositories, and transfer/name-reuse behavior.
observation_vs_inference.inference: A second repository is an independent monotonic witness only if its administrative rollback domain is genuinely separate from the target repository's authority and the Chat writer has durable write authorization without also holding rollback authority. Same-principal placement therefore does not satisfy the required authority separation.

leaf_result.falsification: A second GitHub public repository under the same controlling account/principal is not an anti-rollback authority boundary. Moving the witness to an independently administered repository can separate authority, but the tested route then requires an independently maintained owner/protection/authorization setup or pre-existing external trust anchor, which remains a residual manual/protected/external dependency rather than scheduled-Chat-native closure.
leaf_result.minimal_unresolved_child: A zero-entitlement Chat-writable witness whose rollback authority is outside the target repository administrator/principal domain, while its creation, protection, authorization, recovery and incarnation binding require no separate human/protected/external setup.

quota_cost_dependency_assessment.public_repository_plan_gate: GitHub Free public repositories are sufficient for the storage surface tested.
quota_cost_dependency_assessment.residual_richer_mode_protected_manual_ex: present for any authority-separated second-repository variant because independent ownership/protection/authorization must pre-exist or be established outside this role's scheduled-Chat authority

conflict_check: Single bounded Part86 leaf only; no optional second semantic leaf executed; no scheduler mutation; no forbidden role/downstream/O inputs read.
continuation: Part87: execute exactly one bounded GitHub-public-fork witness leaf using official public documentation plus own clean state only. Test whether a public fork can preserve an append-only minimum-generation/incarnation witness when the target repository is deleted or transferred, and whether target-repository admins lack authority to delete/rewind an independently owned fork. Required negatives: fork owned by the same principal, independent fork owner but connector lacks Contents-write authorization, upstream delete/recreate, fork detach/rename/transfer behavior, branch/ruleset admin rollback in the fork, and any manual/protected setup or second-principal requirement. Accept only if the entire witness lifecycle remains scheduled-Chat-native, zero incremental cost and zero finite monthly/trial/paid quota; otherwise persist the exact remaining authority/setup gap.
